routes.description: Build a cumulative historical inference from early resurrection testimony, the unexpected individual-resurrection claim, Christianity's worldwide expansion, and later cross-cultural visions to Jesus's historical resurrection.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the relevant phenomena are historically supported, resist the principal ordinary and comparative explanations, and jointly make an actual resurrection a plausible explanation of the motion's full evidential pattern.

motionBridge.description: Show why the combined pattern of early appearances, unexpected messianic interpretation, worldwide expansion, and later visions points to Jesus actually rising from the dead.

centralBridges.description: Establish that early and multiple appearance testimony provides historically significant support for encounters with the risen Jesus.
Show that available Jewish expectations do not adequately explain the emergence of the claim that one crucified Messiah had already bodily risen.
Connect Christianity's exceptional expansion and fulfillment of Jesus's stated worldwide mission to the continuing activity of the risen Jesus.
Show that recurring visions of Jesus, especially among non-Christians who convert, are distinctive evidence of continuing risen activity.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Identify relevant differences between the resurrection evidence and allegedly comparable testimony from other religious traditions.
Explain why each evidential line contributes as part of a cumulative case even if no single line independently establishes resurrection.

routes.description: Show that critical historical inquiry cannot infer a physical resurrection from indirect appearance reports, psychologically and socially explicable belief formation, religious growth, or recurring vision traditions.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the offered phenomena remain compatible with ordinary testimonial, perceptual, psychological, social, or comparative religious explanations, leaving resurrection insufficiently established as a historical conclusion.

motionBridge.description: Show that the admissible historical evidence does not overcome ordinary explanations or the probability problem posed by an otherwise unprecedented return from death.

centralBridges.description: Establish that most named appearance claims are indirectly reported and must be tested by the same reliability standards applied to comparable religious testimony.
Explain how perceived postmortem experiences, prior knowledge, psychology, Jewish afterlife concepts, and social reinforcement could generate resurrection belief.
Show that Christianity's influence and expansion demonstrate conviction or institutional success without identifying a miraculous historical cause.
Show that dreams and later visions neither establish the reality of their objects nor uniquely distinguish Christianity from other religious traditions.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Use structurally comparable witness, miracle, growth, and vision traditions to test whether the affirmative applies its evidential criteria impartially.
Maintain the distinction between theological interpretation and the source criticism and probability judgments required for a historical conclusion.

sections.title: Early Appearance Testimony and Source Reliability
sections.rationale: This issue tests the historical basis of the earliest appearance claims, including direct versus indirect testimony, multiplicity, accessibility, and consistent treatment of comparable religious witnesses.

sections.title: Unexpected Messianic Claim and Formation of Resurrection Belief
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether an individual risen Messiah was too unexpected to arise naturally or could emerge from visionary experiences, Jewish afterlife concepts, and communal reinforcement.

sections.title: Ordinary Explanations and Historical Probability
sections.rationale: This issue examines bereavement experiences, mistaken perception, Paul's conversion, cumulative inference, physical regularities, and the evidential standard for establishing resurrection historically.

sections.title: Christianity's Expansion, Influence, and Fulfilled Mission
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether Christianity's worldwide growth and Jesus's exceptional influence support continuing risen activity or merely record the later success of a religious movement.

sections.title: Later Visions and Comparative Religious Experience
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether cross-cultural visions of Jesus provide distinctive continuing evidence or remain nondiagnostic alongside dreams, healings, and vision traditions found in other religions.
